deskreply/detached-worktree-own-repo.note: FIXED (#1901). deskreply no longer refuses a detached HEAD outright: preflight records the branch as none, resolves the HEAD commit, and leaves the own-PR decision to deskkit.CheckOwnPR, which admits a checkout whose HEAD IS the PR's head commit (exact match) under any branch name or none. Every local precondition now passes in the worktree shape the worker-desk and pr-shepherd skills mandate, and the run stops at the public-repo gate, the first step needing GitHub, exactly like the branch-checked-out control. Before the fix this row was unverifiable at exit 6 ('detached HEAD — check out your PR's feature branch first'), and workers fell back to raw `gh pr comment`, which skips deskkit.BodyCheck.

deskreply/detached-worktree-cross-repo.note: A detached worktree at origin/<branch>, in a repo DIFFERENT from the caller's own. Since #1901 the detached-HEAD guard no longer fires, so this row now reaches the SEPARATE cross-repo precondition and refuses at exit 5 ('not this worktree's origin — deskreply only replies on your own PR'), as this note predicted before the fix. That refusal is the intended outcome: a worker replies from a checkout of the PR's own repo, which the own-repo row above now admits.

deskreply/branch-checked-out-own-repo.note: THE HARNESS'S OWN CONTROL for deskreply: the shape the verb was written for. Every local precondition passes and the run stops at the public-repo gate, the first step needing GitHub. If THIS row ever stops being reached-remote, the harness is broken and its verdict on the mandated shape means nothing — read a red here as could-not-check, not as a finding about deskreply.

deskpr-create/detached-worktree.note: deskpr create carries the same precondition shape as deskreply: preflight refuses a detached HEAD at exit 6. A worker in the mandated worktree cannot open its own draft PR through the tool, which is why the fallback row exists in every skill's tool-wiring table.

deskpr-create/branch-checked-out.note: THE HARNESS'S OWN CONTROL for deskpr: local preconditions satisfied, body scanned clean, link trailer checked (example-stream/02) and resolved under --root, worker token minted, PR list read, rate limit passed, stopped at the public-repo gate.

deskpr-create/no-trailer.note: example-stream/02: the link gate is the FIRST local precondition. A body without exactly one `Brief: <stream>/<NN>` (resolving under --root) or `Issue: #<N>` refuses at exit 5 before getwd/preflight and before any network call — the PR→brief edge is data, not convention, and there is deliberately no bypass flag.

deskpr-update/no-trailer-body.note: example-stream/02, update path: update reads the PR's existing body from GitHub; a body without the trailer refuses at exit 5 naming the line to add (the migration-window behavior for pre-trailer PRs — the worker edits the body and re-runs).

deskpr-update/detached-worktree.note: The follow-up-push verb, in the mandated shape. This is the one a shepherd needs most — it is the fix-to-re-review hot path — and it is unreachable from the worktree the skills require.

deskpr-update/ready-flipped-pr.note: FIXED. An approved, ready-flipped PR that has gone stale against a moving main now HAS a sanctioned desk-tools push path: `deskpr update` no longer refuses on !isDraft — it accepts a ready OPEN PR under the same author-owns-branch, bodycheck, rate-limit and public-repo guards as a draft, and this run reaches those guards, stopping at the public-repo gate (the first step needing GitHub) exactly like the deskpr-create/branch-checked-out control. Before the fix this row was refused at exit 5 and the PR sat permanently stuck.

deskpr-create/secret-body-no-override.note: The secret scan refusing a real credential shape in a real binary, at exit 5. The scenario ALSO asserts the refusal message advertises --force-scan-override: a worker left the sanctioned transport because the refusal said 'no override flag by design', and a way through that nobody is told about is a way through nobody takes.

deskpr-create/secret-body-logged-overrid.note: The audited bypass end to end: the same refused body, plus --force-scan-override with a stated reason, proceeds past the scan AND lands exactly one scan_override audit row carrying the tool, the surface digest, the reason and the identity. The scenario asserts BOTH halves — an override that proceeds without logging is the unlogged bypass this scenario exists to replace, not a fix for it.

deskpr-create/desktoken-absent-from-path.note: The cold-shell case: desktoken not resolvable on PATH, exit 6. It shares its exit code with the detached-HEAD refusal above, which is why the two rc=6 causes must be kept distinguishable ('distinguish the two rc=6 causes so the telemetry is readable'). The harness cannot fix the conflation, but keeping them as separate named scenarios makes it visible in the record.
